title: Calder’s Closet
program_note:
A favorite hobby of mine (although seldom indulged in) is making mobiles.  It has been said that anyone who tries to make mobiles either copies Alexander Calder, or makes bad mobiles.  I have long admired Calder’s work, and have looked through many books on or about him.  In one of these books was a picture of Calder walking through his studio, which was covered wall-to-wall and floor-to-ceiling with differently-shaped pieces of sheet metal or stiff wire.  In my mind, from this black-and-white still photograph emerged the sound of pieces of metal clanging against one another, in a beautiful cacophony.  I set to work writing a piece of music which makes use of metallophones—the vibraphone and most of the percussion instruments—to which the harp and piano have been added (since they have, after all, metal strings).

This work, then, is a fantasy on the shapes and movements of Alexander Calder's mobiles, as they spin languidly in a soft breeze or tumultuously in a strong wind.  It  was originally begun in 1990, with revisions made in 1992.  That version won First Prize at the 1st Fukui International Harp Music Awards Competition and was premièred there in August, 1992, and was also performed at the Gaudeamus Music Week Competition in August, 1994.
